ModMetadata.Name: StationGod MCP
ModMetadata.Author: XCeled
ModMetadata.Description:
[h1]Let an AI agent read and run your Stationeers base[/h1] StationGod MCP connects an AI agent such as Claude Code or Codex to your running game through the Model Context Protocol (MCP), the standard way these agents call outside tools. The agent can then read every device, chip, room, network and planet value you could look up yourself, and act on them: write logic, program chips, move gas and items, and build or rebuild cables, pipes, chutes, walls and frames with the checks the game itself applies.
[hr][/hr] [h2]What the agent can do[/h2] [list] [*][b]Devices and logic:[/b] find devices anywhere in the world, read and write their logic values, slots and memory, many at once, and record how values change over time. [*][b]Chips:[/b] read, write, compile, pause, step and restart IC10 programs, including a suit's chip, and set IC Housing pins. With StationeersLua installed, also Lua chips on consoles, computers, tablets and visors, with their errors and print log. [*][b]Your base and planet:[/b] rooms and their air, the planet's atmosphere and weather, plants and their genes, damage, fire risk, water, food, your vitals, the game clock, what you are looking at. [*][b]Items and gas:[/b] find and count items, move them between slots, label and paint structures, move gas between canisters, tanks, pipe networks, landing pads and rooms. [*][b]Solar, dishes and traders:[/b] aim solar panels and satellite dishes, check landing pads, buy and sell with a landed trader. [*][b]Cables, pipes and chutes:[/b] plan a route, lay it, remove it or reroute it. Every piece gets the right shape for its connections, runs follow frames rather than crossing open air, and a run that would join two networks, overload a cable, burst a pipe or push items the wrong way is refused or flagged. [*][b]Upgrades and clean-up:[/b] turn a cable network into heavy or super heavy cable, or a pipe network into insulated pipe, in place; replace junctions that have open ends, merge or split long straights, cut redundant loops and remove dead-end stubs. [*][b]Walls, frames and structures:[/b] swap walls, windows and frames for another kind without opening the room to the air, place any structure a kit builds, and remove structures as deconstruction does. [*][b]Ingot Vault:[/b] with the Ingot Vault mod installed, read a vault's store exactly and move ingots, ores and ices straight in and out of it. [*][b]Blueprints:[/b] with BlueprintMod installed, paste a blueprint at an exact spot and quarter turn, even on a dedicated server with no player, then check or undo it. [*][b]Console:[/b] run the game's console commands and read the console. [/list] Every tool that rebuilds something has a dry run first. The real run holds the game tick, changes everything in one step, takes from your inventory what the game would charge, gives back what deconstruction would, and checks the result afterwards: connections, pipe contents, rooms and air.
[hr][/hr] [h2]Setup[/h2] [list] [*][b]1. Subscribe[/b] and enable StationGod MCP in StationeersLaunchPad. [*][b]2. Install the sidecar,[/b] the small program the agent starts. In the mod's Workshop folder (steamapps\workshop\content\544550\<item id>\Sidecar) extract [b]StationGodMCP.Server-win-x64.zip[/b] (no .NET needed) or [b]StationGodMCP.Server-portable.zip[/b] (needs .NET 8) to a folder outside every mod folder, for example %LOCALAPPDATA%\StationGodMCP\server. [*][b]3. Register it with your agent.[/b] Claude Code: claude mcp add --scope user stationeers -- "<folder>\StationGodMCP.Server.exe". Codex and other clients: a stdio MCP server running that file. [*][b]4. Host a save.[/b] The mod answers only in a game that hosts: turn on Start Local Host in the game's settings (StartLocalHost in setting.xml), then load a save. A client joined to someone else's server gets no answer. [/list]
[hr][/hr] [h2]Settings[/h2] A single local game needs none. StationeersLaunchPad config editor, or BepInEx/config/net.xceled.stationeers.stationgodmcp.cfg: Name in section Pipe, the rest in section Remote MCP (reaching a dedicated server over the network). Read when the game starts. [table] [tr][th]Setting[/th][th]Default[/th][th]What it does[/th][/tr] [tr][td][b]Name[/b][/td][td]StationGodMCP[/td][td]Name of the local pipe. Give a second game or test server on the same machine its own.[/td][/tr] [tr][td][b]Enabled[/b][/td][td]Off[/td][td]Accept sidecars over TCP. Stays off without a secret.[/td][/tr] [tr][td][b]BindAddress[/b][/td][td]0.0.0.0[/td][td]Address the server listens on.[/td][/tr] [tr][td][b]Port[/b][/td][td]8765[/td][td]TCP port.[/td][/tr] [tr][td][b]Secret[/b][/td][td]empty[/td][td]Shared secret every sidecar must send. Sent unencrypted: use a long random value.[/td][/tr] [/table] Each also reads an environment variable (STATIONGODMCP_PIPE_NAME, STATIONGODMCP_REMOTE_ENABLED, _BIND_ADDRESS, _PORT, _SECRET), handy for Docker.
[hr][/hr] [h2]Removing it[/h2] Everything the agent built or changed is ordinary game content and stays. The one thing the mod adds is the StationGod Gateway (a Logic Memory lookalike printed at the Electronics Printer): gateways and their kits disappear from a save loaded without the mod. Nothing else needs doing.
[hr][/hr] [h2]Good to know[/h2] [list] [*][b]Multiplayer:[/b] the mod does its work on the host, where the game's own state lives, and changes reach players the usual way. The host needs it; every player joining needs the same version too, because the Gateway is a new structure. [*][b]Trust:[/b] the agent gets real read and write access to the world, including console commands and device memory. Use an agent you trust, and save first. [*][b]Gateways are optional:[/b] the agent reaches every device in the world without one. A gateway only narrows a call to the devices on its data networks. [*][b]After a game update[/b] the mod checks every game member it relies on at load; a missing one turns off only the tools that need it, and the agent is told why. [*][b]No agent connects?[/b] Look in the BepInEx log for lines starting [b][StationGodMCP][/b]. [/list]
[hr][/hr] [b]Requires[/b] [url=https://github.com/StationeersLaunchPad/StationeersLaunchPad]StationeersLaunchPad[/url] and an AI agent that speaks MCP.
[b]Source, issues and the full readme:[/b] [url=https://github.com/altmank/Stationeers-StationGodMCP]github.com/altmank/Stationeers-StationGodMCP[/url]
Developed with the use of generative AI, and tokens aren't free. Buy me a coffee: [url=https://ko-fi.com/xceled]ko-fi.com/xceled[/url]
ModMetadata.ChangeLog:
v1.4.0 - New vault_contents, vault_deposit and vault_withdraw tools for the Ingot Vault mod: read a vault's store exactly, and move ingots, ores and ices straight into and out of it (from your inventory, a container or the ground, and back into your inventory or any holder's slots) with the vault's own bookkeeping, no chute, door or vend queue. Dry run by default. 77 tools now. - move_item no longer puts an item into an Ingot Vault's display slots, where it would be lost.
v1.3.5 - grid_survey, find_things, looking_at and connections report how a device stands turned (facing, up, Euler angles), in the form place_structure takes, so it can be placed again the same way or turned round. - place_structure's dry run shows where a device's ports would land before it is built. - plan_pipe_route takes an in-line tank or passive vent as a route end (its free end), and the route planners can keep cells or other ports' cells free (reserve_cells, reserve_ports). - move_gas has a dry run: the prediction and checks without moving anything. - label explains that the small in-line tanks cannot be labelled (the game's Labeller cannot rename them); the big ones can.
v1.3.4 - move_gas takes a room as the source or target ({"room_id"} from the rooms tool, or {"room_of"} a thing in it): named gases are taken from every cell of the room in proportion, or spread over its cells by volume, and the reply shows the room's pressure before and after. A room must be given the gases to take, so its air is never emptied by accident.
v1.3.3 - move_gas can take named gases out of the planet's own air (from "planet", delete): the same air Terraforming Reloaded reads, plus its clouds and ice caps. Needs Terraforming Reloaded.
v1.3.2 - Landing pads hold gas: atmosphere_contents and move_gas take any landing pad piece (or the pad network) as the pad's one shared atmosphere, and find_things counts pad pieces as holding gas. - move_gas refuses a move that would damage what receives it: liquid over 2% of a gas pipe network, gas or liquid freezing in a network, or the pressure once arriving liquid has boiled. The reply adds that boiled state.
v1.3.1 - place_structure places batteries, small transformers, vents, pipes, small tanks, valves and other ordinary devices again; they were refused as rocket parts because they may also be fitted in a rocket. remove_structure's rocket check had the same mistake. - Two walls back to back on one face can be placed in one request. - A small device given at a cell's centre that cannot stand there is set down on the floor below (or the face behind a mounted one), as the placement cursor does, instead of being refused for a missing frame. - Positions in messages are in metres (they were ten times too large). - plan_removal on a dedicated server only warns that there is no player to receive the refund. - A tap's changed trunk piece is logged as joined; resolved_networks lists each handle once; a breach through two plates back to back is reported once.
v1.3.0 - Removal checks name the devices a split would cut off from their APC or generator, not just how many networks it makes. - New clean operation remove_redundant: removes every cable or pipe piece no device needs, oldest first, keeping new pieces you name. It finds old and new feeds that meet at a device, which remove_loops cannot. - Runs that stop next to or one cell short of the network they should join are flagged (not_joined); join_trunk adds the missing piece. Route plans check this for their target. - Networks can be named by any piece or device on them, or a device port, so a name stays valid after edits change the network id. - A run started while another job is busy says so with that job's id, or waits its turn with wait: true. Run jobs list the ids of the pieces they built. - Fix: remove_structure no longer calls removing a wall plate on a finished frame a breach, and now catches two plates back to back removed together.
v1.2.0 - Route planners can plan as if old pieces were already gone (assume_removed) and remove them in the same job, so a new run can go where old cable is about to be taken out. - New route preference hidden: the least visible route, inside frames first, then frame surfaces, walls, air. Routes report their new cells by how visible they are. - Bus mode: give a trunk instead of a target, and every start branches from it; the trunk and its drops are one job. Up to 16 starts per plan (was 8). - grid_survey marks cells inside a frame ('i') apart from its surface, lists each network's floating cells, and can show what removing each piece gives back. - New feed_paths tool: which rooms each device's feed passes through from an APC, flagging daisy chains. New plan_removal tool: a removal's refund and split check without doing it. 74 tools now. - Fix: materials given back after a job (walls and frames swapped, cables removed...) were made at the player's position and could hurt the suit. They now go straight into the inventory: matching stacks first, then empty slots, and only what does not fit onto the ground in front of the player.
v1.1.1 - Route rule inside_frames now accepts the top of a frame beam and the outer faces of frames, judged the same way as frames_first and prefer frame_edges; it used to refuse them as the empty cell above. - Rerouting between an APC (or any device on several networks of the kind) and another end no longer fails with not_on_one_network: the network both ends share is used, and an end may name a device port as {reference_id, port}. When no network or several are shared, the error lists each end's ports and networks.
v1.1.0 - New paste_blueprint tool: with BlueprintMod loaded, paste a blueprint at a position and quarter turn you give, as the D.B.P.U. does, with no player needed, so it works on a dedicated server. It also reports progress and undoes. 72 tools now. - New setting [Pipe] Name (or STATIONGODMCP_PIPE_NAME): a second game or test server on the same machine can listen on its own pipe. mod_info reports pipe_name.
v1.0.0 - First release: an MCP server for Stationeers with 71 tools for devices and logic, IC10 and Lua chips, rooms, air, planet, plants, items, gas, traders, solar panels and dishes. - Build and rebuild cables, pipes and chutes, upgrade and clean up networks, swap walls and frames, and place or remove any kit-built structure, each with a dry run, a held game tick and a check afterwards. - Local games over a named pipe; dedicated servers over authenticated TCP.
